AlbumCreditItem.description: One person's credit on a record, mirroring `release_personnel`.
AlbumCreditItem.title: AlbumCreditItem

AlbumUnitBlock.description: One official record as a whole object: what is on it and who made it.
AlbumUnitBlock.title: AlbumUnitBlock

AskFocus.description:
What the visitor was pointing at when they asked: a grid's cell, a year on a song's timeline, or an opened ranked row.

The browser reports it with the question; the server hands it to the model
as a note and lets the IDs it names join the turn's grounded IDs.
AskFocus.title: AskFocus

ConversationTurn.description: A browser-safe projection of one human or final assistant message.
ConversationTurn.title: ConversationTurn

DataChartBlock.description:
A model-selected chart, hydrated entirely from one verified
aggregate_data result.

Every number here is server-computed from that exact result; the
model chose only which aggregation to reference and how to frame it
(title/note). The server derives orientation from the dimension
column's type (temporal -> vertical, else horizontal) and finds the
dimension column itself (the one whose key isn't "value") at render
time, so no field mapping travels through this block at all.
DataChartBlock.title: DataChartBlock

EditorialBlock.description: Prose, viewpoints and comparisons in the model's own words, rendered in one of several forms.

presentation.description: narrative: prose, written as paragraphs. fact_grid: a compact set judged on shared terms, including attributed viewpoints, one item per row. timeline: a sequence, one item per step.
presentation.title: Presentation

EditorialBlock.title: EditorialBlock

EditorialItem.description: One editorial item as the browser receives it.

detail.description: One or two sentences of context or evidence for this item.
detail.title: Detail

follow_ups.description: Up to three topics the visitor might want more about, each a short label plus the specific question it opens when pressed, rendered as chips under 'More about'.
follow_ups.title: Follow Ups

link.description: A link to an outside article or page this item draws on. For a show, performance or record, name it by ID instead and the server links it.

marker.description: A short label that classifies or indexes this item and renders as small type above the subject: a year, a date, a set position, or a category such as 'The skeptical view'. Never the subject itself.
marker.title: Marker

title.description: The specific subject of this item, rendered as its heading: a claim, a viewpoint, a place, a person, or a record you name. Put your assessment in value or detail.
title.title: Title

value.description: Your concise assessment of the subject, such as 'The high-water mark' or 'Looser, faster'. A short value renders as display type; a sentence renders as text.
value.title: Value

EditorialItem.title: EditorialItem

EditorialLink.description:
An outbound link the model attaches to something it wrote.

The server keeps a link only when its URL appeared in material the tools
returned during the same turn; anything else is dropped before rendering.
EditorialLink.title: EditorialLink

EraUnitBlock.description: A stage of a development the composer names, with representative listening.
EraUnitBlock.title: EraUnitBlock

ExperienceGroup.description:
A model-selected relationship between one or more body blocks.

``block_indexes`` preserves the composer's reading order after references
have been resolved. The browser only renders this supported presentation;
it never re-groups or re-orders the material.
ExperienceGroup.title: ExperienceGroup

notebook.description: The research notebook the previous response returned, sent back unchanged.
notebook.title: Notebook

notebook.description: Signed research notebook: what this conversation's tools found so far. Send it back with the next question.
notebook.title: Notebook

FollowUpTopic.description:
A short topic chip the visitor can press, and the full question it stands for.

The chip shows only the label under "More about"; pressing it sends the
question, in the visitor's voice, to start a new turn. Only the composer
writes these; the server never generates one.
FollowUpTopic.title: FollowUpTopic

GridBlock.description:
Two lists and where each pair meets. The model chose the lists, the
order, what opens first, the cells to point at and the words; the server
filled every cell, track, date and venue.
GridBlock.title: GridBlock

GridCell.description: One meeting of a row and a column, every fact from the store.
GridCell.title: GridCell

GridHighlightNote.description: A cell the model pointed at, and what it said there.
GridHighlightNote.title: GridHighlightNote

GridRequest.description:
A visitor's reshape of a grid: the lists as they now stand, plus the
model's headline, note, cell notes and follow-up chips, which the server
hands back with the cells that remain.
GridRequest.title: GridRequest

GuestAppearanceListBlock.description: Guest-show relationships for one resolved person.
GuestAppearanceListBlock.title: GuestAppearanceListBlock

GuestAppearanceSong.description: One song a guest is credited on, from performance_performers.
GuestAppearanceSong.title: GuestAppearanceSong

ListenAction.description: A listening destination attached to the object it plays.
ListenAction.title: ListenAction

ListeningHeroBlock.description:
The page's lead when the answer is best heard: a cover, a name and one Play.

The model chooses the show or record, writes the line and the Play words,
and says where playback starts; the server hydrates identity, the image,
and the playable queue from the server.
ListeningHeroBlock.title: ListeningHeroBlock

PerformanceUnitBlock.description: One rendition as a primary object, with its set context and listening actions.
PerformanceUnitBlock.title: PerformanceUnitBlock

PersonRosterBlock.description:
A complete set of people, organized under one model-chosen heading.

The inventory component for questions that ask for everyone: the model
names the section and chooses who belongs in it; the server supplies each
person's name, roles, show count and span.
PersonRosterBlock.title: PersonRosterBlock

PersonRosterItem.description: One person in a roster: identity and appearance facts from the store, one note from the model.
PersonRosterItem.title: PersonRosterItem

PlayableTrack.description: One Internet Archive track the in-page player can play, in show order.
PlayableTrack.title: PlayableTrack

PullQuoteBlock.description: One sentence the model sets apart, large, as the page's pulled line.

text.description: One sentence, in your voice, that states the idea the visitor should carry away.
text.title: Text

PullQuoteBlock.title: PullQuoteBlock

RankedListBlock.description: The top rows of one aggregate_data result, ranked, with the model's notes on the rows it chose.
RankedListBlock.title: RankedListBlock

RowDetail.description: What a ranked row, bar or roster name opens to: its record's key facts, one play, one question.
RowDetail.title: RowDetail

RowPlay.description: The one recording an opened row plays, chosen by the server from stored signals and tapes.
RowPlay.title: RowPlay

ShowSelectionBlock.description: A clearly attributed selection of shows from one reviewed source.
ShowSelectionBlock.title: ShowSelectionBlock

ShowUnitBlock.description:
One show as a primary object of the answer, hydrated from the store.

The composer supplies the interpretive fields (emphasis, note, highlights,
preferred recording, sources, follow-up topics); date, venue, setlist, guests and
listening actions come from the stored facts.
ShowUnitBlock.title: ShowUnitBlock

SongLengthPoint.description: One performance's length, for the timeline's Length view.
SongLengthPoint.title: SongLengthPoint

SongNeighbor.description: The song just before or after a performance in its set, and whether it ran into or out of a segue.
SongNeighbor.title: SongNeighbor

SongRepresentativePerformance.description:
A model-chosen rendition that gives a song unit an immediate listening path.

On a song timeline it is one of the model's stops, with its label and why.
A stop the server could not resolve keeps only the model's words.
SongRepresentativePerformance.title: SongRepresentativePerformance

SongSignal.description: A voice that picked the performance, or its show.
SongSignal.title: SongSignal

SongYearCount.description: How many times a song was played in one year; a year with none is zero.
SongYearCount.title: SongYearCount

SongYearDetail.description: Every performance of one song in one year, for the timeline's See all.
SongYearDetail.title: SongYearDetail

SongYearNext.description: The song that most often followed this one that year, segue or not.
SongYearNext.title: SongYearNext

SongYearPerformance.description: One performance in a song's year, every fact filled in by the server.
SongYearPerformance.title: SongYearPerformance

SongYearSummary.description: One year of a song's life on stage; a year it was not played has a count of zero.
SongYearSummary.title: SongYearSummary

UnitSource.description: Evidence the composer associated with one unit, resolved to a grounded URL.
UnitSource.title: UnitSource

VersionStripBlock.description:
Chosen nights of one song pairing, drawn to one clock.

The model chose the pairing, the nights, their order and the framing; the
server hydrated each night's venue, date, tape-track lengths and playable
tracks from the server, and the per-year counts when the model asked for
them.
VersionStripBlock.title: VersionStripBlock

VersionStripRow.description: One night's pairing: the two tape tracks the row plays in turn.
VersionStripRow.title: VersionStripRow

post.description:
Rebuild a grid from the library after the visitor adds or removes a list.

The model's headline, note, cell notes and follow-up chips come back
with it; a note whose cell is gone drops away.

get.description:
What a ranked row, chart bar or roster name opens to; library facts only, no model call.

``scope`` is the song a year chart counts, so its years open to that
song's year. It shares the grid's lookup limit and, like a song's
year, may be cached for an hour.

One song's performances in one year for the timeline's See all; library facts only, no model call.

It shares the grid's lookup limit. Library facts change only with a
deploy, so the browser and any cache may keep the answer for an hour.
